# Dune implementation status

## 27 October 2026 — Voice naming Portable Snooper

Voice can name the physical Portable Snooper independently of generic poison
defense. Ordinary plan requirements, prohibitions and the late-defense check
share the canonical matcher; normal Snooper stays distinct. Existing controls
and minimal bot plans use the shared choice. Individual ordinary-card names,
wider interactions and final/deployed acceptance remain open.
[Scope](PORTABLE_SNOOPER_ENGINE_AUDIT.md#named-voice-choice--27-october-2026).

## 27 October 2026 — Semuta after a ready battle preparation

The neutral Semuta opportunity now follows a legal Residual Poison discard
when one combatant has already readied in the open pre-leader stage. The
original selected victim and readiness are preserved through claim or pass,
then the native Poison suffix runs once. Inspected commitments and wider
combinations remain separate; final and deployed acceptance remain open.
[Scope](RICHESE_RESIDUAL_POISON_ENGINE_AUDIT.md#semuta-after-a-preparation-ready--27-october-2026).

## 27 October 2026 — Ecaz same-recipient Duke tenure

A fresh eligible Ecaz Ambassador grant can provisionally convert a current
recipient's other temporary Duke tenure to the ordinary until-battle tenure,
without creating a disc or resetting its battle history. Already-ordinary
tenure remains redundant; Advanced Harkonnen same-holder cases are guarded.
Full combinations and deployed acceptance remain open.
[Scope](ECAZ_DUKE_ACQUISITION.md#same-recipient-temporary-tenure--27-october-2026).

## 27 October 2026 — Ixian stronghold route collection choices

The Hidden Mobile Stronghold's route editor supports provisionally selected
amounts in each visited sector, with native force/pile limits and Sandmaster
deductions. Normal cancellation and Advanced special Karama retain the chosen
amounts. Older omitted choices retain automatic maximum or no collection;
the minimal bots may use that legal default. Foreign-passenger interpretation,
broader interactions and final/deployed acceptance remain open.
[Scope](IX_PROTOTYPE.md#hidden-mobile-stronghold-route-collection-choices--27-october-2026).

## 27 October 2026 — Basic Truthtrance storm-dial comparisons

Upcoming original Basic Storm dials support exact, at-least and at-most
questions. Multiple answers share the real dial's finite legal range, and old
saved exact questions retain their original shape. Native sealed submission,
existing player guidance and minimal AI remain connected. Advanced and wider
combinations, full rules and deployed acceptance remain open.
[Scope](TRUTHTRANCE_TURN_ACTIONS.md#upcoming-basic-storm-dial-choice--27-october-2026).

The bare Basic Richese Semuta profile admits structured scalar, grouped and

The Advanced Emperor's special Karama may return up to three physical
Sardaukar without using the ordinary one-per-turn elite allowance. Native
Tanks, reserve routing and the one-use card cost remain authoritative; saved
historical counters are not rewritten. Normal and other revival sources retain
their own limits. [Source interpretation](RULE_DECISIONS.md#emperor-special-revival-and-sardaukar-limit--27-october-2026).

## 11 October 2026 — Semuta with a bound battle-plan promise

The Truthtrance receipt already carried a battle promise and the integrity
validator already enforced it. The Semuta admission excluded every promise kind
other than none, and a separate guard refused any reaction while a battle existed.
Admitting `kind === 'battle'` and exempting `truthtranceDiscard` from the
battle-presence guard lets an ordinary definite battle answer offer its consumed
card without touching the promise or its enforcement. Submitted/revealed-plan
questions bind no new promise but still offer Semuta, as do ordinary fact answers
during battle; the original checkpoint's automatic-continuation claim was wrong.

The regression fails before (no offer) and passes after, covering claim and
decline, the surviving promise, an illegal-dial rejection, the legal dial, public
history and inventory conservation. Types/lint pass and the 126-case affected
union passes. The fixture needed both combatants marked ready in the shared
pre-leader phase before a plan can be committed; that is existing battle
preparation, not a change to it.

An isolated runtime smoke subsequently exercises unsubmitted, submitted, revealed
and battle-fact answers with claim, all-seat pass and four legal AI profiles
(24 scenarios). Battle plans and history remain unchanged; retired events reject.
The unsubmitted promise rejects dial0 and accepts dial2; the submitted and fact
paths accept the next legal plan without changing the answered plan.

This is local changed-path proof, not complete Semuta or deployed acceptance.
Contracts: [source boundary](SEMUTA_SOURCE_UPDATE_20260907.md),
[discard continuations](SEMUTA_DISCARD_CONTINUATIONS.md).

## 11 October 2026 — Semuta with a bound Truthtrance shipment promise

### Fresh `combined-homeworld-nexus` run and the Auditor custody fix

A fresh `--profile combined-homeworld-nexus --rules both --players all` run
exposed a harness gap rather than a product defect: `tools/sample-custody.ts`
built its expected Traitor deck from the printed leaders only, while Advanced
CHOAM adds its printed extra **Auditor** disc during setup, so every fresh
Advanced all-expansion sample failed at setup with `physical traitor custody`.
The expectation now includes the Auditor for Advanced CHOAM seats.

With that fixed the fresh run completes **2/4** (both Advanced: 6-seat winner
ixians, 5-seat winner ecaz + ixians). The two Basic samples stop at phase 6 on
`Odd-force Basic Occupy awaits the preserved publisher casualty-rounding
ruling` — the same third-party question listed above, not the implemented
rulings. `tests/sample-custody.test.ts` (11 cases) still passes.

## 7 October 2026 — five pending user rulings implemented

The user resolved five recorded rule questions; each is indexed in
`RULE_DECISIONS.md#user-rulings--7-october-2026` and implemented with a focused
regression:

- **CHOAM low-population opening income.** CHOAM's phase-opening income now
  counts as a qualifying collection, so a low-population native Homeworld adds
  its bank increment under the same Inflation multiplier as ordinary charity.
  The previous `requireRule` guard is removed; the projection and the CHOAM
  income notice expose the added bonus. `tests/homeworld-charity-engine.test.ts`
  compares low and non-low Tupile with and without Inflation.
- **Richese exhausted/canceled cache.** `requireRicheseDeclarationCache` now
  rejects only a malformed or negative count, and an exhausted cache runs the
  ordinary pool at its full declared count. A canceled/prevented compulsory
  cache auction sets `cacheCanceled`, restores one ordinary lot and runs the
  pool; the cache offer is skipped whenever no cache lot can run, and the pure
  continuation quote mirrors that. `tests/richese-settlement-preflight.test.ts`
  asserts the one-lot restoration, and
  `tests/nexus-richese-betrayal-engine.test.ts` asserts an exhausted-cache
  Black Market sale now completes.
- **Suk Graduate / Kwisatz Haderach.** Rescued counters count toward Advanced

## 7 October 2026 — administrator failed-attempt history

Rejected administrator authentication and authorization attempts are now
recorded durably in a new additive `admin_attempts` table with a fixed reason
(`invalid_key_format`, `unknown_or_disabled_key`, `missing_session`,
`unknown_or_expired_session`, `role_denied`), the attempt kind, the attempted
role and an already-known account id. No key, key hash, session token, session
hash, request body, origin, address or user agent is stored, and the
unknown/disabled distinction is deliberately collapsed so the lookup cannot
become an account-enumeration oracle.

`GET /api/admin/operations?attempts=1` returns seven-day per-reason counters
plus the twenty most recent attempts, newest first, to a live owner only, with
`no-store` and the same query guard as the other reads. The operations page adds
**List failed attempts** with the counters and the bounded sample, truncating
each account id to eight characters. Recording is best-effort inside the
rejection path, so a rejected request keeps its own answer even when the table
is unavailable; the history never locks out, disables or revokes anything by
itself.

Evidence: `tests/admin-attempts.test.ts` asserts every recorded reason, the
kind/role/account fields, that successful sign-ins and privileged reads record
nothing, that no credential text appears anywhere in the page, the reporting
window, the twenty-row bound and owner-only recheck after demotion, and that a
dropped attempts table leaves the original rejection answer unchanged. The
anonymous HTTP boundary also denies `?attempts=1`. The shared `AdminError` moved
to `db/admin-error.ts` so the recorder and the access module no longer form a
value-import cycle. No game, seat, saved state or deployment changes.

## 7 October 2026 — administrator stalled-decision diagnosis

The owner-only operations page gains **List stalled decisions**: a bounded,
read-only sample of at most ten live rooms whose public pending interaction —
`decision`, `response`, `truthtrance` or `phaseOpening` — has been idle longest,
reported as room code, idle duration, interaction kind, turn and phase. The
aggregate sample adds `stalledRooms` and `oldestStalledChange` for the same
predicate. `GET /api/admin/operations?stalled=1` repeats live owner authority,
answers `no-store`, rejects any other query combination with `400` and stays
read-only: it repairs nothing and pause/close/remove/archive keep their own
audited controls.

Paused, closed, removed and archived rooms are excluded, as are unreadable JSON
states and non-playing rooms. Only public coordination facts are selected — no
hands, orders, private decisions, seat credentials or raw saved state — and the
sample is bounded to ten rows, oldest first. A stall is inferred from the room
write time, so a slow human turn also counts; the sample does not diagnose why a
decision is stuck, disk capacity or backup recoverability.

Owner-only unit coverage asserts the counters, the oldest stalled write, the
bounded oldest-first order, every exclusion boundary, idle arithmetic, the
absence of private content and the owner recheck after demotion. The anonymous
HTTP boundary now also denies `?stalled=1`; the full HTTP integration suite
passes 55/55 against a local build of this revision. No game, seat, saved state,
deployment, public start or played-save conversion changes.

Target: classic GF9 2019 Dune + advanced game + Ixians & Tleilaxu + CHOAM & Richese + Ecaz & Moritani, including optional expansion modules. User additionally requests generated images, animations, AAA polish, a complete navigable rule reference with tooltips/guidance, and addable AI players at Easy/Medium/Hard/Brutal difficulty. The player-facing app must not link to external sites. This is an ACTIVE goal, not a completed implementation.

## Current working slice

- Vinext/React/TypeScript, Cloudflare Workers + D1 via Sites.
- Lobby with faction choice, rooms and shareable eight-character invitations.
- D1 authoritative JSON state with optimistic version checks; private HttpOnly seat cookies hashed in storage; personalized projections strip hidden game information.
- Six base factions, traitor setup, Fremen allocation, prediction.
- Basic nine-phase loop: storm dials, spice blow/Nexus, charity, auctions, revival, shipping/movement, sealed battle/traitor choices, collection, victory.
- Base faction choices now include BG optional free shipments; Fremen ally worm protection, post-Nexus multi-sector worm rides and free ally revival; winner card discards; Harkonnen ally traitor support. Server enforces the designated decision owner.
- Battle preparation has guaranteed Voice → prescience → element answer → sealed-plan steps. The faction owner chooses whether to assist an ally, only the requested element is committed, and prescience values stay private to the two combatants.
- Multi-sector movement and Guild shipments, with single total rounded shipment cost. Ally funding supports private phase-specific pledges, refunds and explicit payment splits; committed bids stay funded. Ordinary spice draws preserve deck order.

Hooks cover ordinary shipment, cross-territory movement, Guild transport, spiritual-advisor arrival and worm rides. No-Field and Face Dancer modules remain outside this implementation. Self/allied entry and moving within the same territory do not open Terror. Existing occupation alone does not trigger it.

The Moritani owner may leave a token hidden or reveal an implemented effect. Robbery transfers half the entrant’s available spice rounded up, or draws before enforcing a chosen hand discard. Sabotage randomly discards once, then offers an optional own-card gift. Only authorized hands are projected; unrevealed identities and random discarded cards do not enter public logs. Reload preserves the stage and never replays shipment payment or the original force transfer. Truthtrance completion reconciles an already-cleared Robbery overflow. Fremen’s summoned-worm interruption now opens its owed Nexus before remaining rides after Terror completes.

## Current reaction and funding design

- `Game.decision` is a single server-gated decision union: advisor / wormProtection / wormRide / battleCards. `spiceResolution` persists resumable worm draws; `wormRides` resolves after all Nexus choices. Existing JSON rooms normalize missing fields on the next action.
- `Game.aid` holds spice earmarked by a donor for its ally in phase 3 or 5. A bid records its exact ally contribution. Unspent funding can be revoked unless committed to the current high bid; remaining funds return at phase end. Projections show only the player’s own pledge and ally credit.
- Harkonnen is an additional traitor voter when allied to a combatant, regardless of whether it holds a relevant card, preserving secret hand information. Resolution waits for its affirmative reveal or decline.
- Printed base PDF is downloaded at `/tmp/dune-rules/base.pdf`, extracted with layout at `/tmp/dune-rules/base.txt`. Reviewed pages 9–12, 16–19 confirm group movement, ally funding, optional discards and faction choices.

- `Battle.preparation` owns Voice/prescience steps. `prescience.value` commits a single element only after an existential legal-plan check, so Voice cannot force an impossible answer. `components/battle-preparation.tsx` owns these action forms. Karama cancellation now covers Voice and prescience. Add Truthtrance on top of these explicit windows.

## Official FAQ priority

The November 2020 official FAQ is indexed at https://www.gf9games.com/dune/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/Dune-FAQ-Nov-2020.pdf although direct fetch is still 403. Use targeted web searches to read its indexed sections. It supersedes the older base PDF mirror where they differ. Implemented: Weather Control and Family Atomics may be played after the dial distance is known but before actual movement. Remaining corrections: bribery is intended as advanced; Karama auction acquisition wording updated; audit simultaneous expansion stronghold victories. Storm-contested occupation is now excluded from victory counts. Truthtrance may ask any game-related yes/no question including current-turn commitments; unknown answers allow another question or later play. Full enforcement will need explicit structured commitments plus handling for freeform questions; do not silently limit its semantics and call it complete.

## Latest windows and cards

- `Game.stormPending` reveals the total before movement; all players confirm and card changes reset confirmations. Weather Control can replace revealed dials.
- `Game.spiceWindow` keeps each base spice blow open for Harvester before Nexus/charity. Harvester doubles new spice only; the old incorrect collection multiplier was removed.
- `Game.response` suspends normal play for a public power use. Every seat may allow; another faction may spend Karama to cancel. Supported: Voice, prescience (before answer), spiritual advisor, Emperor auction income, Harkonnen bonus card. More response kinds remain.
- Auction winner now receives an `auctionPayment` decision: pay bid or use Karama. Holding Karama allows overspice bids; an eligible player may take the current card directly. Full-hand limits still apply. Payment, income and bonus-card resolution are separated.
- Exact official Karama list was retrieved via targeted search `site:gf9games.com/dune/wp-content/uploads/2020/11 "unlimited"`; indexed page 7 gives rules, superseding the April FAQ. Shipment with Karama costs Guild rates paid to the bank (not free); implemented with a benefit for the active recipient, who chooses their own shipment. Remaining base cancellations include Guild rates/transport, Fremen movement. Guild income and Harkonnen ally traitor support now have cancellation windows.
- Rule UI: `/rules` is searchable reference; `/rules/coverage` retains implementation ledger. Data in `game/reference.ts`; client in `components/rules-reference.tsx`; reusable `HelpTip` and TooltipProvider integrated in layout.

- AI: `game/bots.ts` accepts personalized views for candidate selection; authoritative rules filter candidates. `runBots` copies input state and advances up to 96 actions per transaction, with `botsPending` allowing authenticated continuation. Host-only lobby actions manage seats; no player cookie is issued for bots. `game/bot-profiles.ts` supplies UI descriptions without importing the engine into the client.
- Player-facing external hyperlinks have been removed from lobby and rule pages. Research provenance remains in developer documentation. Rule topic deep links open their target details.

- Fremen setup accepts sector-specific allocations and retains compatibility with earlier territory-level setup actions.
- Emperor alliance actions: immediately spendable spice gifts, and up to three extra allied force revivals at two spice each. Both have cancellation windows; canceled uses cost no spice or quota. Extra revivals are tracked separately from normal revival. Gift amounts are projected only to Emperor and recipient.
- Full base-faction reference topics now describe printed starting conditions, powers, allies and special victories. Six advanced-faction reference topics document their powers while clearly marking execution support as planned.

- `game/combat.ts` enumerates casualty combinations matching both dial strength and spice support. Exhaustive independent small-army assignments verify the solver, including the printed Sardaukar example.

- Battle resolution pays support (except a traitor winner), then gives the normal winner a `battleLosses` decision before card discards. Casualty options preserve the player's choice of token types; traitor/explosion losses include all elite tokens.
- Elite revival quota resets at the next turn, not when Revival starts. Ordinary revival, Ghola and Emperor extra revivals share it. November FAQ page 2 explicitly confirms no Ghola/Emperor/Tleilaxu exception.

- Guild alliance transport now includes half-price off-planet shipment, on-planet cross-shipping, and Fremen paid cross-shipment from southern reserves. Only Guild may ship back to reserves. Allied cross-shipping pays the Guild, except the Guild-funded share, which pays the bank. Guild funding of its ally's ordinary shipment goes to the bank; only the recipient's paid share becomes Guild income.
- New primary evidence: November FAQ page 2 allows temporary allied-territory entry during shipping/movement provided the entrant moves out. Current `allowedEntry` still rejects allied destinations; must implement the complete movement obligation without creating unresolvable turns or inventing a voluntary-loss rule. Passing through an ally's territory is already possible.

## Advanced storm/spice and foresight checkpoint

- Each advanced blow has its own discard pile and completes its Harvester/Nexus/ride sequence before the next blow. First-turn worms return after both blows. Additional worm placement is optional; its Karama cancellation blocks further placements for the current turn only.
- Fremen worm survival and optional allied protection have separate response windows before devouring. Only a surviving Fremen group can ride after the Nexus. Cancellation of one protection does not silently cancel the other.
- Advanced Fremen privately forecasts a randomly selected 1–6 storm card after movement. The next turn reveals that card instead of dialing; Weather Control can override it. Foresight cancellation hides the card without changing the distance. Without Fremen, normal dials remain.
- `stormResolution` resumes sector traversal around elite casualty decisions. Half losses round up per exposed group, and repeated laps recalculate against survivors. Legal Fremen reserve shipments into storm damage the arriving group only. Storm-protection responses cover the current storm movement or that individual shipment.
- Atreides auction and movement spice peeks now pause before private revelation. Each auction card gets a fresh response; a full Atreides hand does not suppress its peek. Movement shows one card even with double blow. An empty spice deck refills before foresight, preserving the revealed top card.
- Corrected allied Guild cross-shipment payments using the current GF9 base rulebook FAQ, page 23: all allied shipments pay Guild. The Guild's own contribution still pays the bank (November 2020 FAQ page 2). This supersedes the earlier implementation note saying cross-shipments pay the bank.
- End-of-game fallback is now implemented from base FAQ page 23: Fremen when Guild is absent; highest individual stronghold counts including ties when both are absent. Expansion victory interactions and optional extra-turn ties remain to implement.
- Advanced starts and all expansion starts remain disabled. These tests verify individual rules in advanced fixtures; they do not establish full advanced compliance.

## Guild timing and integrated checks

- `movementRemaining` tracks uncompleted turns independently of fixed storm order. Advanced Guild gets a now/wait choice at each boundary, may take its whole turn first/last/between others, and cannot interrupt an active player. Once Guild completes its turn it is removed from the queue permanently for that phase.
- The first attempt to take an early turn or delay the normal slot has a `guildTiming` Karama response. Cancellation locks normal order for that phase. Allowing a delayed turn grants the timing use; Guild can decide at subsequent boundaries without declaring its eventual position in advance. Flags reset at the next movement phase.
- Allied co-occupation resolution uses actual completed movement turns, which matters when Guild changes order. Temporary allied entry still needs implementation; the current entry check remains restrictive.
- Fixed a pre-existing recursive phase-transition bug: skipping an empty battle phase could invoke spice collection twice. The transition now returns after advancing; a regression test checks the exact per-force collection cap.
- Bot elite revival choices respect the shared one-per-turn limit, and stronger policies deliberately deploy elite reserves. Hard/Brutal scenarios combine the currently implemented advanced storm/spice/combat/timing systems and finish without stalling or violating elite conservation. This is not a claim of complete advanced play.
- Verified current checkpoint: 141 unit/AI/reference tests + 3 persisted multiplayer tests; typecheck, lint and production build pass. No deployment yet.
- Next advanced implementation: advisors and remaining cancellation/special Karama powers, followed by full timing audits. Then all expansion mechanics and full integration.
- Primary base page 13 explicitly resolves blow A and its Nexus before revealing blow B. Its combat example and increased spice-flow rule were retrieved directly from the indexed official GF9 PDF.

## Harkonnen capture checkpoint

- Leader records remain with their original faction. `capturedBy` determines temporary control, and `controlledLeaders` is the common server source for battle validation, prescience feasibility and resolution. This avoids duplicating leaders or losing their death/revival history.
- A winning advanced Harkonnen battle queues capture after casualty and card choices. Harkonnen can decline; acceptance opens a Karama response before any random draw. Only surviving eligible leaders enter the draw, including the just-used leader in the same territory. Then Harkonnen privately chooses retention or execution.
- A `concealed` snapshot preserves outsiders' pre-capture knowledge without exposing the captive's identity through the original owner's leader roster. Captor and owner see actual state; Tleilaxu additionally sees concealed executions, not living captives. Revealed use or revival clears concealment. Turn resets clear obsolete territory markers from both current and concealed records.
- Execution pays 2 spice and places the leader face down, with at least two deaths. Live captives return after one battle; dead captives enter their original owner's tanks. Losing every native Harkonnen leader immediately returns unused captives. Captured leaders can turn traitor and retain their territory restrictions.
- Original-owner revival now treats capture as unavailability when opening a leader revival cycle. Executed face-down leaders remain restricted until their later cycle, with Ghola able to revive them early. KH cycle initialization avoids non-finite values when all native leaders are captured.
- Captive UI, ownership-aware leader selectors, AI capture/use/return policies and a searchable internal capture reference are implemented. Basic/advanced test suites include twelve capture scenarios and JSON round-trip privacy checks.
- Primary sources: GF9 base page 17, November 2020 FAQ pages 5–7, Ix Karama table. CHOAM FAQ page 12 says captured leaders provide only battle-use skill effects; leader skills and further expansion interactions remain to be implemented.

- Verified capture checkpoint: 141 unit/AI/reference tests and 3 persisted multiplayer tests pass. TypeScript, lint and production build pass. No deployment; advanced and expansion starts remain disabled while required rules are incomplete. The goal remains active.

## Guild special shipment-stop checkpoint

- Ordinary off-planet shipments now validate destination, availability, elites, cost and private ally contribution before opening a Guild decision. The decision appears regardless of the Guild’s hidden hand until its once-per-game power is spent. Fremen southern reinforcements and on-planet cross/return transport are excluded; Guild’s own off-planet shipment can also be allowed/stopped under the rulebook’s “any one player” wording.
- `pendingShipment` stores the validated shipment privately. No payment, troop/elite placement, Guild income, intrusion or accompanying advisor happens during the pause. Only the Guild can allow it or spend its actual Karama to stop it. The special power resolves directly and cannot open a normal Karama counter-response. Mutation stays atomic and private projections never include pending funding.
- Allowing invokes the shared shipment commit once and resumes Guild income, then intrusion/advisor choices. Stopping spends Guild’s card and once-per-game power, consumes the shipper’s shipment opportunity, keeps troops/spice/allied credit untouched and leaves ordinary movement available. Any shipment-rate card is tracked privately and returned to its original owner on stop; allowed shipment consumes it normally. Converted Worthless benefits are tested as well.
- **Unverified settlement details:** GF9 base page 14 confirms one off-planet shipment of any one player; November FAQ page 3 supplies phase/once-per-game scope and page 7 establishes Fremen’s reserve immunity. Those retrieved primary passages do not settle retaining/returning rate cards, consuming the canceled shipment opportunity, stopping a separate spiritual advisor, or special-power counter timing. Current settlement is provisional engineering behavior, not a full-compliance claim. Historical/Avalon Hill/tournament and unofficial compilation text must not silently supersede GF9. Audit this before enabling advanced starts and extend it for homeworld/expansion interactions.
- UI provides declared target/count/sector, an allow button and a special-stop button only for actual cards in the Guild’s own hand, plus internal tooltips and rule links. AI at every difficulty resolves the decision from its private projection; higher difficulties protect occupied territories or contest substantial stronghold shipments and preserve allied shipments.
- Fourteen focused tests cover deferred effects, canceled and allowed payment accounting, elite conservation, allied contributions, gifted/converted rate cards, private projection, invalid/bypass attempts, once-per-game scope, movement after stop, basic/Fremen/cross-shipment exclusions, all AI difficulties and JSON-persisted intrusion continuation. Existing rate-benefit shape assertions now include the tracked card internally, while the public view preserves its prior shape.

## Tleilaxu revival commerce checkpoint

- Added shared revival quoting and transactions in `game/revival.ts` and the authoritative engine. Tleilaxu can revive their own forces without the ordinary three-force limit, revive multiple own leaders before all five are dead, and pay half normal prices rounded up. Other factions retain their native revival-cycle and one-leader restrictions. Elite revival remains limited to one per turn across ordinary, Ghola and Emperor-funded revivals.

A canceled limit aborts the transaction without partial revival; a canceled discount restores the normal price and aborts if the payer cannot afford it.

A Ghola treachery play has its separate one-spice reward, including outside the Revival phase. Income cancellation preserves the completed revival. Emperor-funded extra allied forces also pay Tleilaxu, and their separate three-force quota can combine with a granted normal five for eight forces.

## Foreign ghola checkpoint

- Added `game/leader-control.ts` and persistent `Leader.gholaBy`. Every leader remains a single record under its original faction, preserving traitor identity and death history; ghola control overrides native use, and temporary Harkonnen capture overrides ghola control. Multiple acquisitions are allowed up to that pool limit. Face-down executed leaders remain eligible and retain death counts. KH and the Auditor are excluded. The full-price discount cancellation still reprices before any payment or transfer.

Cancellation aborts it without spice or leader mutation and blocks that particular foreign leader for the current turn; another eligible leader can be chosen. Acceptance restores native control and uses the one-leader revival allowance. Stale quotes are revalidated. Ordinary paid revival and Emperor special revival cannot bypass ghola ownership; the Ghola treachery card can revive an existing leader in the acting faction's controlled pool.
- A foreign ghola is unavailable to its native faction for ordinary cycle eligibility. It can fight for Tleilaxu, turn traitor under its original identity, die again and retain the death history. Capture of a foreign ghola now reveals the captured identity to its current controller and Harkonnen; the original faction is an outsider to that capture. Capture logs identify the losing controller. After one Harkonnen use, capture clears and Tleilaxu control resumes.

No player-facing external links were added.

## Ixian setup and auction technology checkpoint

- Wired the future gated Ixian start path to draw one starting card per faction into a private choice. Selecting one shuffles and privately deals the remainder; Harkonnen then draws its extra card from the deck. Pending choice prevents setup completion, is owned by Ixians, and survives JSON serialization. The decision/dealing path is exercised in setup fixtures; public expansion starts still reject unfinished rules and are not claimed end-to-end complete.
- Beginning an Ixian bidding round offers a public Karama window before any cards are drawn or inspected. Allowing draws the eligible-bidder count plus one, then offers a private card/top-or-bottom choice. The remaining cards are shuffled for bidding. Canceling draws only the ordinary count, with no Ixian inspection. A full Ixian hand does not disable this faction advantage; zero eligible bidders skip it. The chosen deck end is publicly logged, while card identity remains private.
- The private projection records an unordered inspected pool. It never exposes the actual next card to Ixians or the pool to other factions. The record includes cards already auctioned and deduplicates an earlier purchase returned through technology; it is not an inferred view of remaining hidden hands. UI labels make this distinction explicit.
- Advanced technology is offered before each card's bidding and before Atreides' independent inspection response. Ixians commit a hand card without seeing the incoming card; a separate Karama window precedes the swap. Declining preserves the option for another card. Declaring uses the round's attempt even if canceled. Successful exchange preserves hand count and makes the replacement the card Atreides can inspect. Canceling pool inspection does not also cancel advanced substitution.
- After an ally purchases a card, the buyer may keep it or request replacement before Emperor income and Harkonnen's separate bonus draw. The replacement response belongs to Ixians and names the buyer publicly; only the buyer sees the purchased identity. Success discards that exact purchase and draws the top deck card privately. Spice payment remains settled exactly once, canceled/declined replacements preserve the purchase, and Karama-paid purchases qualify without Emperor income. Bonus cards do not recursively receive this purchased-card privilege.
- Existing Harkonnen special exchanges can interrupt these windows. A pending offered card that no longer belongs to Ixians skips the stale swap and resumes Atreides inspection; a stale purchased-card decision exposes no replacement and can be declined to settle the sale. These recovery paths preserve card ownership and progress. The exact legality/order of such interruptions remains a primary timing audit rather than certification of every interaction. Bene Gesserit Worthless conversion cancellation restores the suspended private Ixian response correctly.
- Added the `IxTechnology` decision component, setup-aware decision routing, inspected-pool details, tooltip, searchable partial technology rules, updated faction guidance/coverage page, and all four AI policies. AI chooses starting cards, prepares pools, evaluates offered cards against known pool values and replaces weak allied purchases; complete advanced bidding phases terminate through legal private projections at every level. Strategic strength remains uncalibrated.
- Twenty-one new technology tests cover pre-draw cancellation/privacy, eligible/full-hand counts, top/bottom placement, invalid/unauthorized choices, order-independent pool projection, pre-Atreides swaps, one-attempt timing, setup/Harkonnen conservation, paid/free/allied/Harkonnen purchase sequencing, Worthless reactions, stale-card recovery, empty/short decks and every AI level. Short-deck fallback permits a lone available card to auction without removing it; multi-card insufficient-pool behavior remains an explicit rules audit, alongside Richese/other auction modes and exact Amal phase-opening order.
- Primary evidence: publisher Ixians & Tleilaxu p8 (initial and bidding preparation), p9 (advanced substitution and alliance), p11 (explicit Harkonnen extra setup draw), and November 2020 FAQ p7 (three distinct cancelable advantages). Publisher URLs and the genuine mirror remain in the source ledger. No tournament amendments were adopted.

## Truthtrance question-flow checkpoint

- Added `game/truthtrance.ts` with a persistent overlay (`priority → ask → answer`, plus `unknown` for retry/save). The original response, decision, auction, phase opening, storm/spice state and sealed battle remain in place, so completing a question does not reconstruct or replay their effects. The engine rejects unrelated actions while the overlay is active. Setup completion also waits for the overlay to finish.
- Competing declarations are collected before any question is asked, then sorted by storm order. A holder can declare either or both physical copies. - The engine searches full legal completions for an answer, including previous active Truthtrance conditions, Voice, prescience, card-role pairings, controlled leaders, support, elite strength and Ixian half-strength suboids. It only offers answers with a currently legal completion; a sealed plan fixes its answer without exposing its other elements or acquiring new mutable commitments. The search consults the questioned player's private choices and public opponent properties, never the opponent's hidden plan or hand.
- Battle-plan validation enforces all active answers while leaving unrelated elements free. AND/OR conditions preserve alternative completions instead of secretly selecting and locking a witness. Contradictory later answers and prescience values are rejected. The prescience existence check now uses full-plan search when Truthtrance restricts an unshown element, removing the old assumption that all other numeric values can be zero.
- Integration exposed and fixed an existing basic Ixian prescience bug: the API now accepts legal half-point dials for Ixians, matching the existing UI and battle validator. A test specifically reveals 2.5 under a bound Ixian dial.
- A pending Voice response resolves before impossibility releases are considered, so a canceled Voice retains the original answer. After an opposing effect completes, promises are evaluated in their declaration order; an impossible one is publicly released while feasible earlier obligations remain. Canceling Fremen free support and elite strength participates in this search. Voluntary card spending, bribes and aid pledges that would make the actor's still-feasible battle promise impossible are rejected atomically.
- Personalized views expose answer options only to the target, and a legal example plan only to its owner. The React interface adds battle condition fields, public bindings/release status, and a private preview that can populate the editable battle form without sealing it. Tooltips and the internal rules explain the feature and its limits. All four bot levels can choose a feasible answer, filter their candidate plans against existing commitments, and use an authoritative private completion when their heuristic candidate set lacks a required exact dial/support/Kwisatz choice.
- Seventeen new tests cover immutable/public-versus-private state, overlapping Yes/No answers, OR alternatives, dual-role Ix pairs, sealed plans, prescience, pending/canceled/completed Voice, voluntary spice/card evasion, optional Kwisatz flags, duplicate cards and Cheap Heroes, basic Ix half dials, malformed payloads, all four AI levels, Fremen/elite cancellations, and comparison of offered answers against an exhaustive authoritative basic-plan oracle. The full Truthtrance-focused group is 29 tests.
- **Still partial:** feasibility explores currently available plans, not multi-action futures such as reviving a currently dead leader before committing, additional Karama/card sequences, or acquiring a new choice later. Released answers currently stay released; exact revalidation behavior, cancellation timing, self-caused impossibility and multi-promise ordering need a primary-source interaction audit. Guaranteed interrupt opportunities between atomic engine actions also remain unfinished. Do not call this full Truthtrance compliance.
- Source basis remains the official GF9 November 2020 FAQ p8 (current-turn obligations, impossibility, AND/OR, storm order) and base rulebook p23 (Truthtrance during Voice/prescience and freedom to alter unaffected plan components). Tournament amendments requiring reactivation of previously invalid answers are not silently treated as the printed publisher rule.

CHOAM/Richese, Ecaz/Moritani, optional skills/strongholds/homeworlds/Nexus/discovery, AI calibration, complete guidance, generated art/AAA polish and final validated deployment remain part of the active goal. Advanced/expansion starts remain gated.

Assassination immediately selects one random living ordinary native leader, updates its death count and battle-use marker, pays its native strength (Zoal 3), consumes the revealed token and resumes the interrupted entry. A client cannot choose the victim. Missing/unverified rosters, exceptional capture/Ghola custody and empty living pools reject before reveal or RNG. Advanced Harkonnen configurations uniformly reject this reveal so availability cannot disclose concealed captures.

Sneak Attack has a persisted reserve-count decision for zero through five available forces. Positive entry validates the recorded sector, storm and occupancy, transfers reserves without a spice fee or ordinary shipment/movement consumption, and resumes the original continuation. Owner-only limits and unfinished BG/Heighliners combinations are shown before revelation. Zero remains available after revealing; AI retains the hidden token when no positive entry is available. These restrictions identify unfinished implementation, not new official prohibitions.

Fifteen focused force/leader tests cover random selection, all five ordinary discs, Zoal, death history, invalid counts/sectors, resource conservation, reload and duplicate rejection, hidden projections and all four AI profiles including blocked offers. Independent review checked custody, RNG timing and continuation. Full integrated validation: **858 unit tests**, **45 persisted/API tests**, TypeScript, lint and production build pass. Source boundary: `MORITANI_ASSASSINATION_SNEAK.md`.

Atomics/Aftermath, Extortion, Enemy of My Enemy, advanced Assassinate Leaders, exceptional leader pools and combined arrival timing remain unfinished. Full Advanced and expansion starts stay disabled; these isolated QA scenarios do not constitute full-game certification.

## Enemy of My Enemy checkpoint — 2026-09-06

The special Terror alliance branch now has a persisted declaration, Karama response and entrant accept/refuse decision. Acceptance detaches both former partners, refunds only unused escrow attached to broken pairs, clears affected Nexus offers, forms the mutual alliance and returns the token hidden through the existing identity-rotation helper. Already paid shipment costs and committed forces stay unchanged. Refusal immediately enters the ordinary token effect within the same action; Moritani cannot decline again. Karama cancellation preserves the token and permits reveal/decline but prevents repeating that entry’s alliance offer.

Entrant UI branches before every owner-only token lookup. Public stages, names and alliance consequences contain no hidden face; owner controls show why an offer is unavailable. Unsupported mandatory effects and Ecaz are rejected before an offer, so the entrant is never asked to refuse into an unimplemented effect. All four AI profiles complete offer, response, reply, refusal and cancellation paths from private views. Sandtrout does not impose an invented ongoing special-alliance ban.

A related base-rule correction records `allySinceTurn` for Enemy and ordinary Nexus alliances. Newly allied co-occupants are not destroyed at the end of the same turn’s movement; the later mover still loses remaining co-occupants in a following turn if neither leaves. Future entry into an ally-occupied territory remains prohibited.

Fifteen focused alliance tests, independent source/code review, the full **873-unit** suite, **45 persisted/API** tests, typecheck, lint and build pass. An earlier run during test drafting failed only on the new public formation-turn field missing from a test expectation; the completed tests and integrated rerun pass. Browser acceptance survives refresh with hidden token return and exact shipment custody. Source/timing record: `MORITANI_ENEMY_ALLIANCE.md`.

The exact Karama-before-reply ordering is a tested draft using the existing power-response convention; a user clarification is pending because no specialized official timing ruling was retrieved. Full expansion starts remain gated. Atomics/Aftermath, Extortion, advanced Assassinate Leaders, Duke Vidal and other previously recorded scope remain unfinished.

## Duke Vidal shared-leader checkpoint — 2026-09-06

One separate Ecaz-identity disc of strength six now has explicit controller/source/turn custody. It is not appended to any native five-leader roster or traitor deck. Moritani's committed end-of-movement check counts distinct strongholds with actual upcoming battles, excludes Ecaz opponents and uses the existing storm/occupancy geometry; the Hidden Mobile Stronghold counts. A generic Karama window can prevent acquisition, with a once-per-turn marker preventing repeats. A held Duke is not stripped by a new cancellation.

The controller may select Duke in an ordinary supported battle. Death and six-strength bounty resolve on the shared disc; after one battle his controller clears while death history remains. An unused Moritani tenure expires at turn end, and a later qualifying turn can acquire him again. Ecaz permanent custody and unresolved allied-loan return are preserved by the custody helper; no loan-return destination is invented. The next storm clears the shared battle-use marker.

The public original purple/gold component and scrolling inspector show strength, custody, no-Traitor status and complete original-language core instructions. Controller-specific battle choices use explicit shared control, so an Ecaz identity never automatically grants control. Truthtrance battle questions and their readable logs now recognize Duke; traitor questions still reject him. Four integration regressions cover that distinction and legal promised plans.

Verification comprises nine pure custody tests, ten engine scenarios including Basic/Advanced casualties and all four AI candidate plans, four Duke/Truthtrance regressions, independent source/code review, full896-unit suite,45 persisted/API tests, typecheck, lint and build. Desktop browser QA exercises actual end-of-movement acquisition, full inspection, Duke battle use, set-aside status and refreshed second-battle options without Duke. These are bounded component/interaction checks, not complete expansion games.

Advanced Harkonnen configurations and captured/ghola custody remain explicitly unsupported for this acquisition/use slice because they affect the shared capture pool and release destination. Ecaz Ambassador acquisition, loans, Ecaz-only five-spice/Ghola revival and its five-in-Tanks revival threshold remain unfinished. Source details: `DUKE_VIDAL_RULES.md`. Advanced and expansion starts stay gated.

## Ambassador entry and automatic decisions checkpoint (2026-09-06)

Implemented five Ambassador effects end to end: Emperor bank grant, Atreides current-hand snapshot, Harkonnen random held Traitor snapshot (including physical Tleilaxu Face Dancers), CHOAM chosen card sales, and Ixian discard/replacement. Bene Gesserit can copy those supported effects from outside the original six-token supply, regardless current custody zones. Ecaz chooses whether to trigger and its current allied beneficiary; the beneficiary controls its own private choices. Every action binds the persisted event ID and stage. Inspection results remain private snapshots and require no acknowledgement.

The committed entry pauses subsequent work without replaying movement or shipment. Self, ally, advisors and physical-marker faction immunity are applied independently of a copied effect. Cohort replenishment waits until the final triggered effect finishes; BG never re-enters the pool. Exposed-city storm crossings and actual Lasgun–shield explosions return Ambassadors to supply without triggering them. Traitor precedence preserves a token when it prevents an explosion.

Independent review found and fixed two exchange deadlocks: CHOAM cash-in and delayed Truthtrance disposal could otherwise spend the beneficiary’s final required discard. Voluntary interruptions must preserve a legal completion, including queued Truthtrance reservations. Legal interruptions retaining a card still complete through JSON recovery.

Auction payments now execute automatically only when the exact declared own/ally split is funded and no physically usable Karama remains. Genuine payment choices and provisional unfunded recovery are retained. Full-plan inspection has no Finish action; the persistent private inspector also supports an external Atreides ally. Authenticated recovery schedules both legacy decision types and persists only actual changes through the existing CAS fence.
